We propose a novel class of handcrafted parametrised features that encode the structural context of a residue. We also use embeddings from existing protein language models (PLMs) to train the classifiers. We train binary and 3-class classifiers, with the 3-class classifiers providing granular information on the type of fold-switch. In our computations, higher classification performance is achieved for binary prediction as compared to 3-class granular prediction. The handcrafted features perform comparably with the PLM embeddings on our standard test set. A rigorous error analysis by us during the review period revealed a critical data-leakage vulnerability in the metamorphic protein test data. This analysis also revealed that the PLM-based classifier suffers sequence-memorisation bias and fails to generalise to novel fold-switching sequences. On the other hand, one of our domain-informed handcrafted feature based classifier detects fold-switching without relying on sequence memory.

struct-pred.title: Scaling RNA Foundation Models through Iterative Refinement
struct-pred.subject: cs.LG
struct-pred.reason: RNA foundation model with learned iterative refinement raises fitness correlation
struct-pred.abstract: Biological function in RNA is encoded across scales, from local sequence motifs to long-range structural dependencies. Conventional RNA foundation models couple parameter capacity and inference depth within a fixed architecture, prescribing a fixed computation graph for each inference. Here we present Eco-RNA, an 80M-parameter RNA foundation model that makes inference depth adjustable through learned iterative refinement. Its shared, input-conditioned Transformer core refines sequence representations through repeated application. The iteration count is selected after training and controls effective depth at fixed model parameters. We train across recurrent depths with masked reconstruction, state regularization, and a one-sided loss that anchors deeper reconstruction to a shallow reference. On the 70-assay RNAGym fitness benchmark, increasing refinement from one to four iterations raises aggregate absolute Spearman correlation from 0.242 to 0.286, with the gain retained through eight iterations. At four iterations, Eco-RNA surpasses the current SOTA Evo 2 40B on all three aggregate fitness metrics despite 500x fewer parameters. Its iteration configurations advance the compute-performance Pareto frontier among the evaluated models. It also outperforms the evaluated baselines in non-coding RNA family classification, RNA secondary-structure prediction, and chemical probing profile prediction. These results establish internal inference computation as an effective scaling dimension for RNA foundation models.

struct-pred.title: FunFOLD5: Combining Localised Templates and Structural Homology for Accurate Predictions of Biologically Relevant Protein-Ligand Interactions.
struct-pred.subject: Bioinformatics (Oxford, England)
struct-pred.reason: localized template search improves protein-ligand binding-site and pose prediction
struct-pred.abstract: A central challenge in protein-ligand modelling is to predict not only the presence of an interaction, but also the correct ligand identity, binding-site location, and biologically relevant bound conformation. While recent deep learning approaches such as AlphaFold3 and Boltz-2 have demonstrated impressive accuracy in modelling protein-ligand complexes, these methods typically require prior knowledge of the ligand, focus on a single dominant binding pose, and rely heavily on large training datasets. Template-based methods offer a complementary solution by leveraging experimentally resolved protein-ligand complexes to transfer both binding-site architecture and ligand chemical identity, enabling function inference even for uncharacterised or engineered proteins. However, conventional template-based methods are limited by their dependence on global fold similarity, which can miss local binding features critical for ligand specificity. Localised template search strategies may overcome this limitation by capturing conserved pocket-level interactions, enabling more accurate and functionally relevant ligand-binding predictions across diverse protein families. We present FunFOLD5, a template-based method for predicting protein-ligand binding sites. Whereas its predecessor FunFOLD4 relied on global fold similarity to identify templates, FunFOLD5 combines local and global searches, integrating rapid structural template retrieval with a local targeted protocol to improve interaction accuracy. The pipeline combines Foldseek-based template searching, curated ligand annotations from BioLiP2, and ligand superposition followed by spatial clustering to identify associated ligands and consensus binding sites. Benchmarking on blind targets from CASP15 and CASP16 demonstrates robust performance across a wide range of biologically relevant ligands, including nucleotides, metal ions, cofactors, and small metabolites. FunFOLD5 achieved high-accuracy predictions for 81.2% of ligand instances (56 of 69). Importantly, the local targeted protocol consistently improved ligand identification, residue-level recall, and binding-pose accuracy. FunFOLD5 is freely available as a Dockerised pipeline at https://hub.docker.com/r/radiyaman/funfold5_template, providing a scalable and reproducible framework for large-scale protein-ligand interaction analysis and functional annotation. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

struct-pred.title: The structural context of mutations in proteins predicts their effect on antibiotic resistance.
struct-pred.subject: eLife
struct-pred.reason: 3D clustering of resistance mutations across 1350 crystal and AlphaFold structures
struct-pred.abstract: In Mycobacterium tuberculosis, a prevalent and deadly pathogen, resistance to antibiotics evolves primarily through non-synonymous mutations in proteins. Sequence-based analyses can uncover the genetic basis of antibiotic resistance, but these methods focus on primary sequence and often neglect other biological signals, such as protein structural information. We hypothesize that integrating the structural context of mutations improves the prediction of effects on function and phenotype. We curate high-confidence structural annotations for the M. tuberculosis proteome from 1350 crystallography and 2337 AlphaFold predictions, and mutations from over 31,000 M. tuberculosis isolates. We demonstrate that mutations in proteins known to cause resistance are clustered in 3D space, even in proteins where inactivating mutations at any position are thought to cause resistance. We find over 450 proteins in the M. tuberculosis proteome that display signals of clustered mutations, many of which have a known relationship with antibiotic resistance. We show that a supervised classifier trained on 3D distance to known resistance sites alone has an F1 score of 96.5% at classifying mutations as resistance-conferring on a held-out test set. This work demonstrates that protein structure provides useful information for categorizing which variants may cause antibiotic resistance, even when the majority of structures are AI-predicted.

struct-pred.title: STRUCTURAL AND MOLECULAR DYNAMICS ANALYSIS OF HUMAN β-DEFENSIN 1 VARIANTS REVEALS DISTINCT PERTURBATION SIGNATURES
struct-pred.subject: biophysics
struct-pred.reason: structural MD maps perturbation signatures of 93 human beta-defensin-1 missense variants
struct-pred.abstract: Human {beta}-defensin 1 (hBD-1) is a small, disulfide-constrained antimicrobial peptide produced predominantly in the kidney and urogenital tract, where it contributes to epithelial innate defense. Genetic variation in the gene encoding hBD-1 has been associated with altered expression levels and susceptibility to infections, including infection following solid organ transplantation, yet the molecular consequences of coding substitutions in the active, mature form remain largely undefined. Here, we integrate conventional genomics, protein bioinformatics, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics to investigate the molecular consequences of 93 human-observed hBD-1 missense variants. Evaluation of hBD-1 missense variants across sequence-, structure-, and dynamics-based dimensions reveals variant-specific molecular perturbation signatures that complement conventional and static biophysical predictions. By treating naturally occurring substitutions as a perturbation series across a compact defensin scaffold, this study identifies multiple molecular routes through which sequence variation can remodel an endogenous antimicrobial peptide and prioritizes variants for direct structure-function testing. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for investigating how naturally occurring hBD-1 variation may influence peptide behavior and, ultimately, antimicrobial function.

struct-pred.title: Recognition and mechanism of M. tuberculosis cell wall galactan transport.
struct-pred.subject: Nature communications
struct-pred.reason: cryo-EM captures ATP-driven gate-helix movement during Mtb galactan ABC-transporter cycle
struct-pred.abstract: Mycobacterial-derived lipid-linked galactan (LLG) is an essential component of the Mycobacterial tuberculosis (Mtb) cell wall core arabinogalactan (AG), a well-established virulence factor and target of anti-tubercular drugs. Cross-membrane translocation of LLG is energetically unfavorable and is therefore catalyzed by WzmWzt, a prominent member of the polysaccharide ABC transporter sub-family. Here we present cryo-EM structures of WzmWztMtb to uncover critical steps of Mtb LLG translocation. Notably, densities suggestive of the mycobacterial-derived LLG substrates were observed in the structure of WzmWztMtb, indicating that the substrate may bind through two Wzm and two Wzt subunits. This proposed LLG binding is fulfilled by a fully upward extension of the Wzt gate helix, which serves as a critical step to prime Wzt for dimerization. The ATP-bound structure revealed a remarkable downward movement of the gate helix, together with the Wzt dimerization. The third, DDM/ATP-bound structure captured WztWzmMtb in an intermediate state with two DDM molecules in the Wzm central cavity. Using two conditional mycobacterial mutants for functional analyses, we have identified residues on the Wzm N-terminal interface helix (IFN) and on the Wzt helical domain are essential for LLG recognition and translocation in vivo. These data provide a clear structural basis for the development of Mtb cell wall targeted therapeutics for global tuberculosis treatment.

ml-method.title: Autonomous AI agents discover reverse transcriptases with tandem repeat arrays
ml-method.authors_short: Yoon, P. H., …, Durrant, M. G.
ml-method.subject: bioinformatics
ml-method.reason: autonomous LLM agents surveyed 1.9B protein clusters, discovered a novel tandem-repeat RT family
ml-method.abstract: Metagenomic databases hold vast quantities of unexplored genetic material that can seed tools for biotechnology and medicine, but discovery is limited by our ability to examine sequence data at scale. Here, we show that large language models (LLMs) in an autonomous harness can alleviate this bottleneck and surface novel molecular systems. We deployed Claude Code instances to survey reverse transcriptase (RT) loci across 1.9 billion protein clusters. Among the top candidates were array-associated RTs (ART), a novel family of jumbo-phage RTs coupled with an array of ~200-nucleotide units and a dedicated partner gene. Session transcripts show that Claude identified the ART family by directly examining its DNA sequences and recognizing the atypical repeats, a behavior attributable to specific Mythos 5 internal signals that respond to repeated DNA. ART arrays are highly expressed and appear as discrete units during Staphylococcus phage infection, suggesting an RT system directed by a repertoire of distinct RNAs. These findings indicate that LLMs can autonomously detect anomalies and drive analyses to initiate biological discoveries.

ml-method.title: Reinforcement Learning via Fixed-point Flow Matching
ml-method.subject: cs.LG
ml-method.reason: data-free fixed-point flow matching enables RL fine-tuning of flow policies
ml-method.abstract: In maximum entropy and behavior-constrained reinforcement learning (RL), the optimal policy is given by a Boltzmann distribution. Generating samples from this distribution can be challenging, as it is often complex and multimodal. While flow policies trained with flow matching provide a powerful framework for representing such distributions, they traditionally rely on access to training data, which is generally unavailable in online RL. To address this limitation, we propose fixed-point flow matching (FFM), a data-free procedure for training and fine-tuning flow policies in RL. FFM leverages the target flow identity to formulate the actor update as a fixed-point iteration, utilizing a flow-matching-style regression objective where the critic's action gradients serve as regression targets. We show that the optimal policy is a fixed point of this iteration. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that FFM effectively fine-tunes pretrained flow policies in the offline-to-online setting and enables efficient and accurate training of flow policies from scratch in online RL. These results establish fixed-point flow matching as a principled approach for learning expressive flow-based policies without requiring training data.

ml-method.title: On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models
ml-method.subject: cs.LG
ml-method.reason: analyzes self-conditioning and embedding-geometry levers in continuous diffusion LMs
ml-method.abstract: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) promise to bring the benefits of continuous flow modelling to language, including accelerated sampling and controllable generation. The field has grown rapidly, and the capabilities of CDLMs have begun to rival those of discrete diffusion. Yet, unlike for continuous modalities such as images or videos, our grasp of the levers that matter when training CDLMs remains limited. In this work, we focus on two of these levers, namely self-conditioning and embedding geometry, and shed light on some of the mechanisms behind them, which in turn suggest cheaper and more effective designs. We begin by showing that self-conditioning corrects a train/inference mismatch by exposing the model to inference-like states that are otherwise rare during training. These gains can be recovered without an extra forward pass by a two-level interpolant, coined $\mathrm{DoubleCat}$, which improves TinyGSM accuracy more than threefold. Self-conditioning also aids in recognising tokens dominated by large-norm Gaussians$\unicode{x2013}$an issue known as token identifiability. To address it directly, we introduce discrete reveals to $\mathrm{DoubleCat}$, yielding $\mathrm{SemiCat}$, which achieves discrete diffusion-level performance on TinyGSM, reaching $49.94\%$ with standard training hyperparameters and a tuned sampler. At the $1.7$B scale, $\mathrm{SemiCat}$ outperforms discrete diffusion on four of six likelihood-based evaluations, and surpasses one-hot flows on unconditional generation. On embedded spaces, we find that cross-entropy drives embeddings towards a geometry whose decoding error rate closely matches the one-hot one. We briefly explore a range of further options, such as hybrid corruption processes and noise schedules, including asynchronous ones. We believe this exploration can help the community better understand and advance the design space of CDLMs.

ml-method.title: Some remarks on the connection between generative diffusion and optimal transport
ml-method.subject: stat.ML
ml-method.reason: entropic-OT view explains mode-speciation transition in diffusion vs flow matching
ml-method.abstract: We discuss three simple connections between generative diffusion and optimal transport. First, the joint law of the data and of their Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noising is, at every time, the solution of an entropic optimal-transport problem, at a temperature set by the noise level. Backward diffusion can consequently be read as an annealing which gradually decreases the entropic regularization. Second, we study the speciation transition--how the modes of the data distribution emerge during generation--and compare how it happens in diffusion and flow matching with respect to optimal transport. Using Gaussian mixtures as high-dimensional example, we show that the dynamical instability through which diffusion and flow matching separate the modes becomes, for optimal transport, an exponentially thin boundary layer at the beginning of generation, which is rounded by entropic regularization. Third, considering a generic forward dynamics with a general confining potential, we show that the backward process driven by the score also satisfies a drift-based variational principle whose minimal cost is the entropy difference between initial and final distributions.

ml-method.title: Opening the Black Box of Classifier-Free Guidance via Information Bottleneck
ml-method.subject: cs.LG
ml-method.reason: information-bottleneck theory finds critical stage to activate classifier-free guidance
ml-method.abstract: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) is a standard technique for improving conditional generation in diffusion models, yet its activation schedule is usually selected heuristically. In practice, most existing CFG-based methods rely on a pre-defined activation policy throughout inference, while recent dynamic variants often depend on hand-designed schedules without a principled theoretical explanation of when conditional information is most useful. In order to understand how the informational relevance between conditioning inputs and the score function evolves over the course of generation, we explore when guidance should be activated from an information-theoretic perspective. In this work, we formulate the diffusion trajectory as a time-dependent information bottleneck and show that the effectiveness of conditional information is not uniform throughout sampling, but becomes significantly stronger after a critical stage characterized by a Fisher-information balance condition. Motivated by this insight, we propose a training-free dynamic CFG strategy for inference. Rather than prescribing a fixed schedule in advance, our method constructs a stochastic process from conditional and unconditional score statistics and activates guidance when the estimated guidance gain crosses a prescribed threshold. This yields an adaptive activation rule that aligns condition injection with the underlying generation dynamics, while also recovering interval-based guidance as a limiting special case. Extensive experiments across diverse architectures and tasks, demonstrate that our method is effective, robust, and broadly applicable. Beyond empirical improvements, our framework provides an interpretation of dynamic guidance methods and a principled foundation for inference-time control in conditional diffusion models.

ml-method.title: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
ml-method.subject: cs.LG
ml-method.reason: transformer learns in-context diffusion score operator, generalizes without retraining
ml-method.abstract: Diffusion models typically learn the generative dynamics of a single target distribution or a family of distributions indexed by conditioning variables fixed during training. This limits their ability to adapt to a previously unseen distribution from only a small set of examples. We introduce an in-context solution operator learning framework for diffusion models, in which each target distribution is treated as a task drawn from a meta-distribution and is specified at inference time by an empirical context set. Our method learns an in-context score operator that maps the context samples, a noisy query point, and the diffusion time to the task-dependent score, enabling reverse-diffusion sampling on unseen tasks without retraining or parameter updates. A key observation is that the task-dependent score admits a Gaussian-kernel conditional-mean representation. Its empirical Nadaraya--Watson approximation can be represented exactly by a model in our constructed transformer class, providing a principled foundation for the proposed query-dependent attention architecture. The operator is trained through amortized denoising score matching across task distributions. We establish generalization-error bounds that quantify the effects of the context size, the numbers of training tasks and within-task samples, model complexity, and intrinsic and ambient dimensions. Numerically, we evaluate the method on a range of scientific and visual datasets, including Navier-Stokes, ERA5 climate data, QuickDraw sketches, and Food-101. The results show that the proposed method performs well on relatively simple task families, while its performance degrades as task complexity increases, thereby illustrating both the promise and the limitations of in-context learning for diffusion models.

ml-method.title: MORAD: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Objective Rewards for RNA Inverse Design
ml-method.subject: cs.LG
ml-method.reason: online RL trains shared backbone-conditioned policy for RNA inverse design across six objectives
ml-method.abstract: We introduce MORAD, an online reinforcement learning framework for backbone-conditioned RNA diffusion models that trains a single shared policy across diverse target backbones. Structure-conditioned RNA inverse design seeks nucleotide sequences compatible with a target three-dimensional backbone, yet existing reinforcement learning approaches either optimize a separate policy for each target backbone or rely on offline preference optimization, leaving online post-training of a reusable backbone-conditioned model largely unexplored. MORAD combines backbone-conditioned group sampling, group-relative reward normalization, and a forward-process diffusion objective. Beyond existing RL rewards that primarily target tertiary structural quality, MORAD jointly optimizes six measurements spanning tertiary geometry, base pairing, ensemble behavior, and sequence composition. To aggregate these heterogeneous objectives despite differences in scale and optimization direction, MORAD maps each measurement to a bounded desirability score and combines them with a weighted geometric mean. Compared with a tertiary-structure-only reward, this multi-objective formulation improves 10 of the 11 evaluation metrics that have a preferred direction. Applied to pretrained RIDE, MORAD improves GDT-TS by 16.0% (from 0.3300 to 0.3827) and pairing MCC by 19.4% (from 0.6110 to 0.7295), while reducing normalized ensemble defect by 27.5% (from 0.3906 to 0.2830). On the test set, MORAD outperforms RiboDiffusion, gRNAde, and RDesign across tertiary structural accuracy, secondary-structure pairing, and thermodynamic quality, establishing a new state of the art in structure-conditioned RNA inverse design.

ml-method.title: Spanning Diffusion and Flow-based Posterior Sampling via Exact Gaussian Conditioning
ml-method.subject: cs.LG
ml-method.reason: exact Gaussian-conditioning Kalman update generalizes plug-and-play guided sampling across priors
ml-method.abstract: Flow-matching and diffusion models are increasingly used as priors for linear inverse problems, however, most methods are bespoke to one class of trajectory prior. Plug-and-play methods have been proposed, however these implicitly decorrelate the guided trajectory, resulting in broad priors that can struggle when data is sparse. This work proposes $β$-Flow: a general plug-and-play method indexed by a correlation parameter $β$ that generalises over flow, diffusion, and decorrelated priors, and a confidence parameter $κ$ that controls how strongly the path distribution is enforced. Each step requires only one forward evaluation of a denoising network, followed by a Gaussian conditioning step. This step is an exact Kalman update that is not dependent on network gradients. We show that many existing guided samplers can be interpreted as instances or approximations of our method, each implicitly using a different trajectory prior and operator in place of the Kalman gain. From this viewpoint, we provide a qualitative comparison of methods in terms of their implicit biases and assumptions. We demonstrate consistently state-of-the-art level performance across 7 inverse problems over 4 datasets in terms of PSNR and SSIM. Moreover, we demonstrate the utility of this prior control, by showing that confident high correlations (strict priors) work best when observations are less informative, while low correlation is preferred when observations are more informative, reflecting the complementary roles of the prior and likelihood in Bayesian inference.

ml-method.title: AI-guided discovery for low-resource peptide engineering using evolutionary scale modeling
ml-method.subject: bioinformatics
ml-method.reason: ESM2 embeddings plus Gaussian-process active learning for low-data peptide engineering
ml-method.abstract: Data scarcity is a major bottleneck in artificial intelligence (AI)-guided peptide engineering, where experimental training sets often contain only tens to a few hundred sequences, and it is difficult to judge in advance whether a protein language model (PLM) will effectively guide iterative discovery before committing to wet-lab work. Here we present SCARSE, a machine learning framework that couples ESM2 protein language model embeddings with Gaussian process regression. Benchmarked across 24 diverse peptide and small-protein datasets spanning substitution and indel variants, antimicrobial peptides, and hemolytic peptides, SCARSE significantly outperformed hand-engineered descriptor baselines on substitution and indel tasks in low-data regimes (20-500 training samples) and performed comparably on short non-mutant peptides. In active learning simulations it consistently prioritized high-performing candidates, discovering up to 7-fold more top-tier peptides than random sampling. Cross-validation (CV) R2 correlated strongly with final active learning performance (Pearson r = 0.80-0.84), and evaluating on as few as 50 labeled peptides reduced CV R2 variance enough for it to serve as a practical, data-efficient criterion for assessing model suitability before iterative screening. SCARSE thus provides an early diagnostic indicator for active learning success and is freely available as an open-source Python package (pip) and through an interactive Hugging Face Spaces web interface.

ml-method.title: Your Discrete Graph Diffusion Model is Secretly Memorizing
ml-method.subject: cs.LG
ml-method.reason: discrete graph diffusion models show conditional memorization of training graphs
ml-method.abstract: Discrete graph diffusion models (GDMs) corrupt the graph structure by adding noise independently to nodes and edges under a Markovian noise model. In the unconditional setting without node features, an equivariant denoiser trained on a single graph is able to generate novel graphs and sample-level metrics such as edge overlap and WL kernel similarity find no evidence of memorization. In this work, we challenge this view and show for the first time that graph diffusion models indeed exhibit memorization. Analyzing the reverse diffusion trajectories of GDMs trained on two-block stochastic block models (SBMs), we find a strong train-data bias: the model recovers a corrupted training graph almost perfectly compared to a held-out test graph. We term this conditional memorization, as it surfaces only when the reverse trajectory is conditioned on a corrupted training graph and is not apparent during inference. It coincides with a growing generalization gap, where the training loss improves as the loss on held-out graphs degrades, and it cannot be mitigated by early stopping. The onset of memorization always precedes the emergence of community structure in the generated graphs, thus every checkpoint earlier produces structureless graphs. This behavior holds across all node sizes we test.

wetlab-method.title: Ab initio CryoEM maps minimizing preferred orientation problems in heterogeneous mixtures: ReconSIREN
wetlab-method.subject: bioinformatics
wetlab-method.reason: deep learning ab initio cryo-EM framework minimizes preferred-orientation artifacts in heterogeneous data
wetlab-method.abstract: Cryo-Electron Microscopy (CryoEM) Single Particle Analysis (SPA) is pivotal for elucidating protein structures and their conformational dynamics. Several critical steps are required to obtain accurate maps. First, the \textit{ab initio} relative orientations and shifts between images must be determined. Second, the common issue of specimens presenting a preferred orientation should be adequately addressed. Third, all of the above must account for particle flexibility and sample heterogeneity. Additionally, these steps are interrelated, making the search for all these parameters a real challenge when considering convergence robustness. In this context, we present ReconSIREN, a novel deep learning framework that addresses the key steps outlined before in an \textit{ab initio} manner while greatly minimizing one of the most important practical burdens in SPA, namely the errors introduced in the CryoEM maps by the existence of preferred orientations; the latter is achieved by a change of the optimization approach that avoids the so-called ``attraction problem'', and by the introduction of a new type of geometrical priors. It does so fully \textit{ab initio}, using deep learning training/inference steps without resorting to more traditional optimization approaches, and generating highly accurate initial reconstructions. We present maps as both homogeneous (consensus) maps and a full conformational landscape for analyzing flexibility and heterogeneity. Thanks to its Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, ReconSIREN distributes the estimation workload across independent experts, improving optimization efficiency and simplifying the process.

wetlab-method.title: Structural thermodynamics by cryo-EM resolves minute energy differences in heterogeneous protein complexes.
wetlab-method.subject: biophysics
wetlab-method.reason: cryo-EM classification plus thermodynamic modeling resolves kT-scale pairwise interaction energies
wetlab-method.abstract: Hetero-oligomeric protein complexes play crucial roles across biology, providing combinatorial diversity and context-specific functionality in membrane receptors, molecular chaperones and beyond. Yet, existing methods are limited in their ability to resolve and quantify the assembly energetics of complex biomolecular populations. Here, we introduce a comprehensive method combining iterative 3D classification, error-rate quantification via simulated particles, and global thermodynamic modeling to extract interaction energies from cryo-EM data. Using hexameric cruciferin (the primary rapeseed storage protein) as a model, we reconstruct a 1.83 [A] structure and distinguish three highly similar 50 kDa isoforms. We resolve the complex compositional heterogeneity of the hexameric species at the single-particle level and fit a global binding model revealing pairwise interaction energies between isoforms differing by fractions of the thermal energy (kB T ). This method offers a powerful, broadly applicable tool to characterize the compositional heterogeneity and energetics of biomolecular complexes.

wetlab-method.title: CryoFAST: A Fab-Aided Cryo-EM Workflow for High-Resolution Structure Determination of Sub-50-kDa Protein Targets
wetlab-method.subject: biophysics
wetlab-method.reason: Fab-fiducial workflow enables cryo-EM structures of sub-50-kDa drug targets
wetlab-method.abstract: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) plays an increasingly important role in structure-based drug discovery (SBDD) by revealing target protein-ligand interactions at the molecular level, but its application has largely focused on large- and medium-sized protein complexes. Many therapeutically important targets are smaller than 50 kDa and remain highly challenging for cryo-EM analysis because of low signal-to-noise ratios and difficulties in particle alignment. Here, we describe cryoFAST, an integrated workflow that couples ligand-compatible Fab discovery and structure-guided computational maturation with biochemical triage, fiducial-complex assembly, and single-particle cryo-EM. Through phage-display screening and/or AI-guided design, we developed high-affinity Fab binders of approximately 50 kDa that stabilize the target without disrupting ligand-target interactions and then assembled Fab-target complexes for cryo-EM analysis. Using the therapeutically relevant extracellular domain (~20 kDa) of interleukin-4 receptor (IL-4R) as a proof of concept, we determined its cryo-EM structure at 2.74 Angstrom resolution and established a framework for elucidating ligand-binding modes. This workflow provides a practical, efficient, and potentially broadly applicable route to the structural characterization of small protein targets that are otherwise challenging to study. By extending the applicability of cryo-EM to high-value but technically challenging small targets, cryoFAST may open new opportunities for structure-based drug discovery.

wetlab-method.title: Single-molecule reaction chambers reveal intramolecular protein kinase activation
wetlab-method.subject: biochemistry
wetlab-method.reason: DNA-origami single-molecule chambers resolve cis vs trans kinase autophosphorylation
wetlab-method.abstract: Many protein kinases, ubiquitous signal transducers across all kingdoms of life, are activated by phosphorylation of one or more conserved residues in their activation loops. This reaction is widely considered to be intermolecular (trans) in nature, dependent on the transient dimerization of two kinase domains. However, since the substrate, product and reaction chemistry are identical, bulk solution kinase assays cannot distinguish between intra- and inter-molecular reactions. Discriminating between these two mechanisms is crucial because they impose different requirements on the cell for acute, high-fidelity signal transduction. Using single-molecule reaction chambers fabricated from DNA origami, we show that the paradigmatic insulin receptor kinase (IRK) undergoes intramolecular (cis) autophosphorylation with kinetics indistinguishable from those in free solution. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the bacterial serine/threonine kinase protein kinase B (PknB) undergoes intramolecular autophosphorylation, allosterically stimulated by intermolecular (trans) interactions. Our findings establish that intramolecular activation loop autophosphorylation is not only possible, but likely an ancient and conserved feature of protein kinase signaling. More broadly, our work provides new tools for single-molecule enzymology.

wetlab-method.title: Autofocusing molecular simulations for integrative structural biology of broad conformational ensembles
wetlab-method.authors_short: Antila, H. S., Miettinen, M. S.
wetlab-method.subject: biophysics
wetlab-method.reason: automated force-field finetuning satisfies 82 NMR order parameters simultaneously
wetlab-method.abstract: Integrative structural biology seeks molecular descriptions consistent with complementary experimental measurements. A particular challenge arises for molecules whose broad conformational ensembles resist description by a few representative structures, such as natively unfolded proteins and fluid-phase biomembrane lipids. Although molecular simulations can generate such ensembles, their simultaneous agreement with a large number of experimental constraints is commonly prevented by model inaccuracies. Here we introduce autofocusing as an approach that integrates experimental information by automated finetuning of the physical model generating the ensemble. We demonstrate it for a fluid bilayer of the phospholipid POPC, for which no existing force field has simultaneously reproduced the complete set of 82 NMR C-H bond order parameters. Autofocusing brings all the 82 within experimental uncertainty while preserving agreement with independent small-angle X-ray scattering measurements and retaining or improving agreement with untargeted NMR relaxation rates and effective correlation times, thus supporting its description of membrane structure and dynamics beyond the calibration targets. The resulting simulations challenge a long-standing two-state interpretation of phosphatidylcholine headgroup structure, instead supporting a broad conformational ensemble poorly represented by crystal-derived conformers. These results establish autofocusing as a practical approach to constructing experimentally grounded conformational ensembles while retaining the computational tractability of classical molecular dynamics.

wetlab-method.title: Purification-free cryo-EM reveals endogenous assemblies from minute tardigrade samples
wetlab-method.subject: biochemistry
wetlab-method.reason: purification-free cryo-EM with long-read cDNA assignment resolves assemblies from crude extract
wetlab-method.abstract: Tardigrades are minute animals renowned for environmental stress tolerance, and their remarkable biology has motivated extensive molecular studies using biochemical and biophysical approaches. Yet the native structures of endogenous macromolecular assemblies in tardigrades remain largely inaccessible, in part because only limited biological material is available. Here we show that purification-free single-particle cryo-EM, guided by long-read cDNA sequence assignment, can recover multiple endogenous assemblies directly from crude extract of a wild-derived Macrobiotus cf. shonaicus culture. We reconstructed a dimeric vitellogenin (Vg) particle at 3.10 [A] resolution, a previously uncharacterized tardigrade ferritin at 3.09 [A] resolution, and a low-resolution ribosome map. The Vg particle is a glycosylated and metal-containing assembly with structural evidence of proteolytic processing and contains lipid-like densities occupying a broad chamber whose walls include N-linked glycans. The ferritin structure revealed a divergent C-terminal helix that lines a mineral-like density observed at a position corresponding to previously described mineralization sites in ferritin-family cages. These results establish purification-free cryo-EM as a route to structural analysis of endogenous macromolecular assemblies from minute animal samples. In tardigrades, this approach provides a foundation for future state-dependent structural studies, including desiccation, rehydration and reproduction.

wetlab-method.title: SCKAnalyzer: A Web Tool for Single-Cycle Kinetics Analysis and Simulation
wetlab-method.subject: biophysics
wetlab-method.reason: free web tool fits single-cycle BLI/SPR kinetics data without surface regeneration
wetlab-method.abstract: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and biolayer interferometry (BLI) are well-established label-free analytical technologies used to determine biomolecular interaction rates (ka, kd) and equilibrium constants (KD). While assays historically rely on multi-cycle kinetics (MCK), this approach requires intermediate surface regeneration, risking sensor degradation and increasing reagent consumption. Single-cycle kinetics (SCK) avoids regeneration by sequentially injecting increasing analyte concentrations. However, implementing SCK workflows on biosensor platforms like the OctetRR8 BLI instrument (Sartorius) remains a challenge due to the lack of built-in or online data analysis tools. To address this, we introduce SCKAnalyzer, a free, user-friendly web application designed for processing and fitting SCK datasets. SCKAnalyzer accepts column-based text files and native raw BLI data (.frd format) from Sartorius instruments, performing data pre-processing and non-linear fitting to a 1:1 interaction model. Additionally, it offers advanced simulation capabilities that allow variable association and dissociation durations across sequential injection steps, a feature absent in existing platforms such as BiacoreTMSimul8. The performance of SCKAnalyzer was experimentally validated using a 3-step SCK method (SCK3) for DNA/RNA duplex formation on a Biacore T200, as well as 4-step (SCK4) and 5-step (SCK5) methods for DNA/DNA duplex formation on an OctetRR8 BLI instrument. Binding parameters (ka, kd, KD) derived from SCKAnalyzer showed excellent agreement with values from established proprietary softwares such as Biacore T200 Evaluation Software v3.2.1 and BIAevaluation v4.1.1. SCKAnalyzer provides a practical alternative to MCK, reducing probe consumption and extending SCK utility across biosensor platforms. SCKAnalyzer is available at sck.iecb.u-bordeaux.fr (source code: github.com/synthaze/sckanalyzer).

wetlab-method.title: A modular DNA toolkit for single-molecule biophysics
wetlab-method.authors_short: van der Torre, J., …, Dekker, C.
wetlab-method.subject: biophysics
wetlab-method.reason: modular DNA toolkit builds up to 100kb user-defined sequences for single-molecule assays
wetlab-method.abstract: Long, customizable DNA molecules are an essential tool for in vitro single-molecule biophysics. Most studies still rely on the {lambda}-phage genome, which has a fixed sequence, a non-uniform GC distribution, and limited options for modification. To overcome these limitations, we developed a modular DNA (ModDNA) toolkit that integrates in silico sequence design with cloning, to create long (up to 100 kb) DNA molecules with entirely user-defined sequences. We used a computational workflow with curated databases to design a motif-depleted sequence backbone, into which any desired sequence can be inserted at any position. Golden Gate assembly then builds these sequences into constructs, which we extend iteratively in defined increments up to 100 kb. We show precise placement of local features, e.g. a fluorophore, a bound protein, and a DNA-origami structure, and illustrate the construct's utility in single-molecule visualization assays, including DNA loop extrusion by human condensin I. ModDNA offers a scalable, sequence-programmable alternative to {lambda}-DNA and other restrictive substrates. More broadly, the motif-aware feature-free design connects single-molecule biophysics to emerging efforts in machine-guided regulatory-sequence design and synthetic-genome engineering, where controlled programmable sequence context is increasingly essential.

wetlab-method.title: Tracking Without Linking or Localization: Single-Photon Tracking
wetlab-method.authors_short: Xu, L. W. Q., …, Presse, S.
wetlab-method.subject: biophysics
wetlab-method.reason: single-photon framework tracks fast biomolecules directly from binary image stacks
wetlab-method.abstract: Mobile biological particles, ranging from biomolecules to viral capsids, often diffuse faster than 1m2/s, resulting in severe motion blur in conventional millisecond-scale imaging. Shorter exposures capture faster dynamics, but quantizing the per-pixel signal at such exposures eventually degrades our ability to localize particles at all. In the extreme case of binary (1-bit-per-pixel) output--where moving from 8-bit grayscale to 1-bit corresponds to a 255-fold faster acquisition rate--no existing tracking method applies, since all of them rely on intensity-based localization that binary data cannot supply. We therefore introduce single-photon single-particle tracking (SP2T), a framework that bypasses localization and linking by estimating particle numbers and trajectories directly from the full 1-bit image stack. We demonstrate SP2T on single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays, which deliver microsecond exposures over a large field of view (512x512 pixels) and explicitly account for detector-specific artifacts such as hot and cold pixels. We validate the method against programmed fluorescent bead and organic dye trajectories, and apply it to two biological systems, aerolysin and ganglioside GM1. Together with simulation, these experiments reveal that longer exposures bias diffusion coefficient estimates (by up to 70% for particles diffusing at 5m2/s) and distort jump-distance distributions, underscoring the need for photon-by-photon tracking in fast-diffusion regimes. Evaluating the likelihood on a GPU further delivers more than a 50-fold speedup over a CPU implementation when compared on datasets of the same frame size and number of frames, enabling multiplexed tracking for crowded particles. Together, these advances establish SP2T as a robust, data-efficient route to unbiased particle tracking at microsecond temporal resolution.

wetlab-method.title: Atomic structure and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from Escherichia coli by cryo-EM and solid-state NMR.
wetlab-method.subject: Science advances
wetlab-method.reason: cryo-EM and solid-state NMR together resolve MscL gating intermediate dynamics
wetlab-method.abstract: Mechanosensitive channels are central to cellular responses to membrane tension, yet the structural basis of their gating remains incompletely understood. Here, we determine the structures of wild-type and Gly22→Ser (G22S) mutants of MscL from Escherichia coli (EcMscL) by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) in peptide-based lipid nanodiscs and complement them with solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements in liposomes to capture their dynamics in a native-like membrane environment. The cryo-EM structures reveal a closed conformation, whereas analysis of the low-threshold G22S mutant by NMR uncovers widespread conformational changes in both cytoplasmic and periplasmic regions. These data indicate enhanced dynamics and conformational heterogeneity in the mutant, revealing the early transitions from the closed toward the open state. Together, our results establish a synergistic framework integrating cryo-EM and NMR to resolve both structure and dynamics of mechanosensitive channels, and identify lipid-protein interactions as key determinants of MscL gating and mechanosensitivity. Our study further provides a quantitative benchmark for computational investigations of mechanogating and lays the foundation for the rational design of channels with tunable gating kinetics.

immunogen.title: Immunogenicity and Structure of a Stabilized HIV -1 clade C Env from a Pediatric Elite neutralizer in Complex with an Autologous bnAb
immunogen.subject: immunology
immunogen.reason: ferritin-NP and SOSIP immunogens from pediatric elite-neutralizer Env, cryo-EM with bnAb
immunogen.abstract: Introduction: The envelope (Env) glycoproteins derived from circulating viruses in elite[ndash]neutralizers (ENs), who naturally develop potent broadly neutralizing antibody (bnAb) responses, serve as a potential template for HIV - vaccine design. Here, we investigated the immunogenicity and structure of a clade C HIV -1 Env trimer (330) derived from the pediatric elite -neutralizer AIIMS_330. Methods: The 330 Env was engineered as SOSIP.664, NFL.664, and multivalent ferritin -nanoparticle (NP) immunogens. Biophysical and antigenic properties were assessed using HIV -1 trimer-specific bnAbs and non-neutralizing antibodies. Immunogenicity was evaluated in rabbits immunized with Addavax-formulated SOSIP.664, NFL.664, or ferritin NP immunogens (n = 4), with an adjuvant only placebo group (n = 2). Structural characterization was performed by cryo[ndash]electron[ndash]microscopy (cryo -EM) using the autologous Env 330 SOSIP.664 trimer in complex with the bnAb 44m. Results: The 330 Env trimers exhibited native - like antigenic properties, high thermostability, strong binding to trimer - specific bnAbs, and limited reactivity with non[ndash]neutralizing antibodies. Immunization of rabbits elicited strong autologous neutralizing antibody responses together with modest heterologous Tier -1 neutralization. Autologous neutralizing responses were significantly higher for ferritin -NP (P = 0.019) and SOSIP.664 (P = 0.048) than for NFL.664, with no significant difference between ferritin -NP and SOSIP.664 (P = 0.681). A 5.1 [A] cryo -EM reconstruction of the autologous Env 330 SOSIP.664 -44m complex revealed native -like presentation of the N332 -V3 supersite. The structural analysis further suggested the interacting Env contacts E293, R32, K337, and K446, along with glycans N332, N326, N442, and N448 with the bnAb -44m. We identified R327 of the conserved GDIR -motif and the N332 glycan, within the V3 -loop, as neutralizing determinants on the 330 Env, with a fold reduction of 116, on testing the mutant 330 viruses with autologous bnAb 44m. Discussion: Pediatric elite-neutralizer AIIMS_330 derived Env trimers represent structurally and antigenically well characterized clade C immunogens with ability to elicit strong autologous neutralizing antibodies, with modest heterologous Tier-1 neutralization. Together, these findings advance our understanding of clade C Env antigenic variability. Further, the structural and immunological insights support the potential utility of AIIMS_330 derived Env as an antigenic probe and may inform future rational design of Clade C HIV-1 vaccines and structure-guided strategies for eliciting neutralizing antibodies.

immunogen.title: Lymphatic constraint of germinal centers optimizes protective antibody responses.
immunogen.subject: Immunity
immunogen.reason: lymphatic remodeling constrains germinal-center size to optimize antibody responses
immunogen.abstract: Immunization strategies are central to pathogen control, where efficacy relies on antigen distribution and inflammatory context. Lymphatic vessels are necessary conduits for antigen transport that actively remodel in peripheral tissues and draining lymph nodes (LNs) in response to their inflammatory context. In this study, we found that inhibiting viral-induced lymphatic remodeling in skin and LNs prompted germinal center (GC) expansion but, paradoxically, decreased the protective antibody response. While GCs scaled proportionately, larger GCs failed to support proliferative bursts consistent with clonal selection due to impaired T-B cell interactions. Accordingly, follicle and GC size are evolutionarily conserved across diverse mammals despite increased LN size. Lymphatic vessels controlled GC size through two coordinated processes: lymphatic remodeling in infected skin limited viral transport to the LN, while the resulting permissive environment in the LN supported perifollicular lymphangiogenesis that constrained GC expansion.

immunogen.title: A multivalent mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine containing eight hemagglutinin antigens elicited broad neutralizing antibody responses and protected against influenza A virus challenge in swine.
immunogen.subject: Journal of virology
immunogen.reason: 8-HA multivalent mRNA-LNP vaccine protects pigs against influenza challenge
immunogen.abstract: The diversity within H1 and H3 subtype influenza A viruses (IAVs) in swine prevents effective vaccine control approaches with inactivated whole-virus vaccines. We addressed the challenge of controlling co-circulating hemagglutinin (HA) clades of swine IAV with the development of a multivalent messenger RNA (mRNA)-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccine expressing eight HA proteins to maximize genetic coverage. We applied a computational approach to select eight HA genes that represented 95% of the observed IAVs detected in the United States between 2022 and 2025. Piglets were vaccinated and boosted intramuscularly with either individual HA mRNA-LNP or an 8-HA multivalent mRNA-LNP. Serum was collected to evaluate systemic antibody levels. Twenty-one days post-boost, pigs were challenged with a field-relevant H1 1A.3.3.3-c3 IAV strain. The 8-HA multivalent mRNA-LNP vaccine induced neutralizing antibodies against all eight antigens, and vaccinees were protected against lung lesions, with lesion scores similar to non-challenged animals. Homologous monovalent vaccination significantly reduced IAV detection in nasal secretions and in the lungs. Heterologous monovalent vaccination was not cross-protective but did not induce vaccine-associated enhanced respiratory disease. We provide evidence that monovalent and multivalent mRNA-LNP influenza vaccines elicited neutralizing antibody responses in pigs and protected against viral challenge. The versatility and capacity for rapidly updating the mRNA-LNP vaccine platform make it an appealing tool to improve animal health and minimize the circulation and diversity of IAV in swine.IMPORTANCEInfluenza A virus (IAV) is an important respiratory pathogen in swine, and zoonotic transmission of swine strains to humans remains a public health risk. Control strategies against IAV in swine herds rely heavily on biosecurity measures and vaccination. However, the antigenic diversity of IAV circulating in swine challenges current vaccination programs, and there is a need for broadly protective vaccines or platforms that can rapidly update components to reflect circulating diversity. mRNA-LNP vaccines have emerged as promising vaccine platforms, offering simultaneous delivery of multiple antigens, rapid development, scalable manufacturing, and potent immunogenicity. In this study, we assessed the immunogenicity and protective capacity of monovalent and multivalent mRNA-LNP vaccines encoding eight representative IAV hemagglutinin (HA) antigens. To our knowledge, this is the first study to objectively select multiple representative endemic swine IAV strains by quantifying genetic diversity within the phylogeny and to apply this selection to rationally design and evaluate a multivalent HA mRNA-based influenza vaccine in the swine model.

immunogen.title: AI-Driven Design of Next-Generation Immunoinformatics Multi-Epitope Subunit Vaccine Targeting the Most Virulent Mpox Proteome: A Structural and Kinetic Validation Framework
immunogen.subject: bioinformatics
immunogen.reason: in-silico multi-epitope Mpox vaccine design pipeline, no experimental validation
immunogen.abstract: The resurgence of the Mpox virus (MPXV) highlights the urgent need for scalable, mutation-resistant countermeasures. Slow development timelines hinder traditional empirical vaccine discovery, while conventional vaccinology often yields high false-positive rates because it relies on static, linear sequence-based screening. These classical informatics filters consistently fail to predict physical structural stability or the dynamic presentation of immune cells under physiological conditions, creating a distinct translational gap between computational design and in vitro efficacy. To address these limitations, here we engineered an advanced, AI-augmented vaccine discovery pipeline targeting the most virulent components of the MPXV proteome. We systematically screened eight critical viral targets essential for replication, membrane morphogenesis, and host-cell entry to map highly conserved T-cell and B-cell epitopes. Moving beyond standard heuristic filtering, we implemented a high-fidelity deep learning validation layer: ESM-2 protein language models (pLMs) were deployed to calculate pseudo-perplexity scores across chimeric linker junctions (EAAAK, GPGPG) to guarantee structural naturalness, MHCflurry ensemble models successfully verified active intracellular antigen presentation, and structure-informed graph neural networks (GNNs) simulated the physical node-attention dynamics of the immune synapse. Finally, recurrent neural networks (RNNs)-driven mRNA kinetic modeling optimized translation initiation rates and minimum free energy profiles during in silico cloning. This multi-layered pipeline successfully yielded three structurally refined, multi-epitope vaccine constructs optimized for maximum global population coverage. ESM-2 structural validation confirmed exceptionally low perplexity scores at structural junctions, indicating that the engineered chimaeras have native-like stability and a minimized risk of proteolysis. GNN-based immune synapse modeling demonstrated highly stable binding kinetics and robust binding free energies between the target epitopes and human HLA alleles. Furthermore, RNN kinetic optimizations established that the cDNA sequences are optimized for high-yield expression in heterologous expression hosts without risk of ribosomal stalling or translational bottlenecks. This study establishes a deep learning-augmented framework that bridges the gap between theoretical sequence optimization and biopharmaceutical scalability. By validating the structural naturalness, real-world immunogenicity, and manufacturing kinetics of our vaccine chimeras, this framework presents a robust, proactive paradigm for rapid vaccine architecture against emerging orthopoxvirus threats.

immunogen.title: HIV remodels germinal centers through T follicular helper cell loss
immunogen.subject: microbiology
immunogen.reason: HIV depletes germinal-center Tfh cells, altering GC architecture independent of CD4 count
immunogen.abstract: T follicular helper cells (Tfh) within germinal centers are among the most permissive cells for HIV infection and serve as a critical part of the viral reservoir. Given the key role of Tfh in affinity maturation and the production of plasma cells and memory B cells, an understanding of this critical viral reservoir is fundamental not only for cure strategies but also for understanding immunodeficiency in people living with HIV (PLWH). Using rare clinical specimens from PLWH, we demonstrate that HIV causes both a change in the cellular composition of germinal centers and changes in their overall architecture in ways that are consistent with the immunodeficiency seen in PLWH, independent of their CD4 count. We note a significant decrease in the number of GC Tfh cells and an increase in the number of follicular CD8 T cells in lymphoid tissues obtained from PLWH. Our data further show that GC size is decreased both by HIV and with increased age. Single-cell RNA sequencing data demonstrate that HIV acutely decreases the expression of Tfh B-cell support pathways and disrupts Tfh expression of cell trafficking receptors. Additionally, in a lymphoid organoid model of acute infection that forms GC-like structures, these findings are recapitulated, suggesting that New Approach Methodologies could be germane to understanding the impact of HIV on the reservoir and immunodeficiency. This study describes previously undocumented remodeling of the germinal center niche in PLWH, providing insight into the immune microenvironment of a key HIV reservoir that may help inform future cure strategies.

immunogen.title: BLIMP1 shapes germinal center B cell clonal diversity by gating chromatin accessibility during light-to-dark zone transition
immunogen.subject: immunology
immunogen.reason: Blimp1 restrains germinal-center clonal dominance by gating BCR-signaling chromatin accessibility
immunogen.abstract: Germinal center (GC) B cell responses are defined by many positive regulators of affinity maturation, but few components that restrain clonal dominance, notably Nr4a1, are known. We reveal an unsuspected role for Blimp1 (Prdm1), a plasma cell determinant, as a feedback regulator of affinity maturation. Single cell RNA-seq and B cell receptor (BCR) seq showed that B cell specific Prdm1 loss drives an exaggerated GC reaction with larger clones, increased somatic hypermutation, and greater clonal dominance, independent of Nr4a1. Single cell chromatin profiling with base-resolution modeling indicated that Blimp1 represses expression of BCR-signaling genes, gating chromatin accessibility at ISRE, EICE, NFKB, and Oct motifs. In the absence of Blimp1, enhanced BCR signaling augments activities of transcription factors that promote G1/S transition during light-zone (LZ) selection and fuel dark-zone (DZ) expansion. Thus, Blimp1 attenuates BCR signaling and constrains the LZ to DZ transition, fine-tuning clonal competition thereby maintaining repertoire diversity.

immunogen.title: Long-term immunoprophylaxis by TLR9 ligand mediates macrophage-ILC cross-talk against respiratory viral infection.
immunogen.subject: Science advances
immunogen.reason: intranasal CpG-schizophyllan complex gives 100-day innate antiviral protection via macrophage-ILC crosstalk
immunogen.abstract: Rapid development of host immunity is critical during the emergence of viral outbreaks when vaccines are not yet available. Here, we demonstrate that CpG oligodeoxynucleotide-schizophyllan complex (K3-SPG) induces antigen-independent, long-term protection against lethal respiratory virus infection. A single intranasal administration successfully enhanced host resistance to infection for as long as 100 days posttreatment. Mechanistically, we observed a lung-restricted biphasic innate activation of macrophages and innate lymphoid cells. Early protection was mediated by CD11b+CD11c+ macrophages (DP MΦ) and monocyte-derived interstitial macrophages (IMΦ). Late protection was mediated by innate lymphoid cells that were epigenetically reprogrammed, suggesting that two distinct innate immune subsets contribute to the maintenance of disease tolerance in the lung microenvironment. Deficiency of TLR9 or TNF-α abrogated innate activation and protective immunity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that adjuvant-induced prophylaxis is a promising approach to enhancing host resistance against respiratory virus infection, involving the biphasic cooperation between innate immune cells in the local tissue.

immunogen.title: In silico subtractive genomics and reverse vaccinology approach reveal outer membrane proteins OMP47 and LptD as dual-purpose drug and vaccine targets in Pasteurella multocida Pm70
immunogen.authors_short: Khan Chowdhury, A. R., …, Elias, S. M.
immunogen.subject: bioinformatics
immunogen.reason: in-silico subtractive genomics identifies vaccine/drug targets, no experimental validation
immunogen.abstract: Drug targets and vaccines for bacterial diseases are challenging to develop. Computational subtractive genomics and reverse vaccinology offer a viable substitute for conventional drug and vaccine development approaches. In recent years, Pasteurella multocida, a Gram-negative pathogen responsible for severe infections in humans along with major diseases in livestock and poultry, has developed resistance to multiple drugs. As a result, there is an urgent demand for research into reliable, efficient, highly potent, and cost-effective strategies to combat the rise of Pasteurella multocida infections. To address this, the present study integrated an in silico subtractive genomics and reverse vaccinology workflow to pinpoint proteins with potential value as both drug and vaccine targets. From the complete Pasteurella multocida Pm70 proteome, we identified 446 proteins that had no similarities with human proteins, out of which 129 were found to be essential for the pathogens survival. These 129 proteins are therefore potential candidates for drug development. Further metabolic pathway analysis, virulence potential, subcellular localization, and structural analyses revealed two outer membrane proteins, namely, 47 kDa outer membrane protein and lipopolysaccharide-assembly protein LptD, as promising candidates for therapeutic development. Subsequent antigenicity analysis revealed both outer membrane proteins as potential vaccine targets, exhibiting highly favorable antigenicity scores. Candidate B- and T-cell epitopes were systematically mapped from these two targets based on antigenicity, immunogenicity, toxicity, and allergenicity potential and only high-confidence epitopes were assembled using adjuvants and class-specific linkers to construct the final multi-epitope vaccine (MEV). The designed MEV construct was demonstrated to be highly antigenic, non-toxic and non-allergenic to humans, while possessing favorable structural and physicochemical properties, and exhibited strong binding interactions with human toll-like receptors with minimal molecular deformability. Although further experimental validation is recommended to fully assess their efficacy, the present study establishes a solid foundation for the development of novel therapeutics and vaccine candidates against P. multocida, ultimately contributing to the reduction of its rising infections.

delivery.title: One Scaffold, Many Targets: Fully Modified RNA Nanostructures for Multi-Gene Silencing Beyond the Liver
delivery.subject: molecular biology
delivery.reason: fully modified vehicle-free RNA nanostructures enable multi-gene silencing beyond the liver
delivery.abstract: Therapeutic siRNAs are a major clinical modality for hepatic gene silencing, but efficient extrahepatic delivery and multi-gene modulation remain significant barriers. Nucleic acid nanotechnology offers programmable assembly, but conventional structures suffer from enzymatic instability in vivo . Here we report fully chemically modified RNA nanostructures (FMRNs): a vehicle-free platform entirely composed of stabilized therapeutic nucleic acids that integrate structural precision with metabolic durability. Following systemic administration, FMRNs exhibit enhanced pharmacokinetics and extrahepatic accumulation, with in vivo behavior influenced greatly by hydrodynamic size rather than molecular weight. Using triangular and square geometries, we demonstrate programmable control over siRNA stoichiometry to achieve sustained, simultaneous silencing of up to four genes from a single entity. Nanostructure assembly alone drives productive delivery, especially to heart and muscle, matching lipophilic conjugation. Furthermore, cerebrospinal fluid administration reveals that larger FMRNs improve central nervous system distribution and retention revealing physicochemical parameters that impact brain exposure. FMRNs establish a modular and effective platform combining improved pharmacokinetics, extrahepatic delivery, and multi-gene silencing for complex diseases.

delivery.title: Physical Basis Of pKa Shift For Ionizable Lipids In An LNP-like Environment
delivery.subject: biophysics
delivery.reason: MD free-energy calculations reveal composition-dependent pKa shifts in LNP-like lipids
delivery.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are a leading drug delivery platform for mRNA or other nucleic acid-based therapeutics. LNP platforms are typically composed of ionizable aminolipids, phospholipids, sterols, and lipids tagged with polyethylene glycol. The ionizable aminolipids are typically cationic at low pH, allowing them to encapsulate negatively charged mRNA. The pH at which the ionizable head groups change charge states, the apparent pKa, is crucial to understand the characteristics and formulation of LNP. However, this is difficult to measure as the apparent pKa differs from the pKa of the aminolipids in bulk solution due to the complex chemical and charge environment. In this study, we use molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with alchemical free energy perturbation to calculate the pKa shift as a function of lipid composition, treating LNP-like and vesicle-like environments. Our results show that the pH-dependent structure of the systems affects the trends in pKa shifts in complex ways, driven by factors including surface electrostatics and lipid internalization. Our all-atom simulation protocol allows us to efficiently estimate the apparent pKa of LNP-like models formed with novel ionizable aminolipids and estimate how it will change with composition.

delivery.title: Predicting viral host range for reverse zoonosis surveillance
delivery.authors_short: Irvine, E. B., …, Reddy, S. T.
delivery.subject: bioengineering
delivery.reason: deep learning plus yeast-display RBD library predicts viral reverse-zoonotic host range
delivery.abstract: Zoonotic transmission of viruses has triggered major outbreaks throughout history. However, human-to-animal transmission, or reverse zoonotic transmission, also represents an underappreciated public health threat. Reverse zoonoses can establish novel animal reservoirs that fuel viral evolution and enable eventual spillback into humans, underscoring the importance of defining viral host range. Current approaches for host range prediction are limited. Experimental methods are retrospective and rely on brute-force testing in a small number of models, whereas computational approaches often lack experimental grounding. Here, we present a platform that integrates high-throughput experimental screening with deep learning to predict viral host range from sequence. We screened a yeast-displayed SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain library against 15 ACE2 orthologs from diverse species, and deep sequenced the ACE2-binding and non-binding populations to generate an atlas of 8.8 million unique RBD:ACE2 interaction measurements. These data were used to train a transformer-based deep learning model that predicts RBD:ACE2 compatibility across animal species from sequence alone, and generalizes in a zero-shot manner to ACE2 orthologs not observed during training. Critically, the model pairs each prediction with a distance-based uncertainty estimate, allowing hundreds of candidate species to be triaged by both predicted host compatibility and confidence. This framework enables the rapid prioritization of animal species for SARS-CoV-2 surveillance and provides a general strategy for anticipating viral host range.

delivery.title: A minimally modified AAV9 variant (AAV9fyhr) for enhanced CNS gene delivery by intra-CSF administration.
delivery.authors_short: Garza, I. T., …, Gray, S. J.
delivery.subject: bioengineering
delivery.reason: directed evolution yields AAV9 variant with enhanced CNS delivery via CSF
delivery.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) mediated gene therapies continue to show promise for the treatment of genetic diseases. However, delivery and safety still represent significant prohibitive barriers restricting translation of these delivery modalities to humans. We describe a novel AAV9 variant, AAV9fyhr or FYHR, identified from screening a controlled randomization point mutation AAV9 library in mice and nonhuman primates followed by directed evolution of in vivo CNS-derived libraries screened in human iPSC differentiated cortical neurons. Capsid variants of interest were identified by coupling long read sequencing and computational structure modeling. Structure-function analysis of our lead candidate reveal that two targeted amino acid changes are sufficient to result in beneficial pleiotropic effects across viral stability, cell surface attachment, and gene delivery. We developed a novel multiplexed barcoding reporter system, enabling a time and cost-effective option to gather spatially resolved single cell capsid validation data in mice and nonhuman primates. When administered intrathecally, AAV9fyhr exhibits 2-to-6-fold higher gene delivery across several tissues in the CNS while minimally altering the tropism to peripheral tissues in comparison to AAV9. These findings demonstrate the potential of whole capsid engineering for the rational development of translational next generation AAV capsids.

delivery.title: Bovine H5N1 influenza viruses have adapted to more efficiently use receptors abundant in cattle
delivery.authors_short: Hassard, J. A., …, Peacock, T. P.
delivery.subject: microbiology
delivery.reason: H5N1 HA mutations enable bovine NeuGc-glycan receptor engagement in dairy cattle
delivery.abstract: Sustained mammal-to-mammal transmission of high pathogenicity H5N1 avian influenza viruses is reshaping the host range of these pathogens. One of the longest-running mammalian transmission chains involves the B3.13 genotype circulating in U.S. dairy cattle which was detected in early 2024. Genomic analyses revealed selection and rapid fixation of haemagglutinin mutations D104G and V147M. We demonstrate, via glycomic profiling, that bovine tissues, including the mammary gland, are enriched in N- and O-linked glycans capped with N-glycolylneuraminic acid (NeuGc), a sialic acid which is not synthesised by humans and birds, which instead express only N-acetylneuraminic acid (NeuAc). Early cattle H5 viruses poorly recognised NeuGc, but D104G and V147M enabled efficient engagement of both NeuAc- and NeuGc-containing receptors. These mutations enhanced replication in bovine mammary tissue without major attenuation of replication in human lung and primary nasal epithelial cells. NeuGc-driven receptor adaptation therefore promotes viral fitness in cattle without majorly changing zoonotic risk. Deep mutational scanning was able to identify alternative haemagglutinin substitutions that confer NeuGc usage and represent surveillance markers for emerging cattle H5 lineages. Finally, structural analyses suggest a potential molecular mechanism for the dual binding of the cattle-adapted viruses.

delivery.title: Rational Design of 5' UTRs for Optimized mRNA Expression and Cost-Effective, Rapid Analysis of Capped mRNA
delivery.subject: bioengineering
delivery.reason: engineered 5' UTR enables probe-free mRNA capping and poly(A) QC assay
delivery.abstract: In vitro-transcribed (IVT) messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics require rigorous quality control of 5' capping efficiency and 3' poly(A) tail length, both of which constitute critical quality attributes (CQAs). Current analytical workflows for these CQAs rely on hybridization with nucleic acid probes and biotin-based affinity purification, which constrain throughput and increase per-assay cost. Here, we report a rationally designed 5' untranslated region (5' UTR) that sustains high translational efficiency while enabling probe-free, one-step purification for rapid quantification of capping efficiency and poly(A) tail length distribution. This approach exploits a strategically engineered 5' UTR incorporating a purine-only RNase A-resistant fragment terminating at a single pyrimidine cleavage site, together with a translation-enhancing element comprising an N6-methyladenosine (m6A) deposition motif and an 18S rRNA complementarity sequence. This dual-function design accommodates GA-rich sequence segments without compromising mRNA translational output. Compared with conventional probe- and biotin-dependent workflows, the present method substantially reduces cost and processing time and is compatible with simultaneous detection of segmented AmGn poly(A) tail variants. This integrated platform provides a simplified, probe-free and construct-universal for high-throughput in-process control (IPC) of mRNA therapeutics.

delivery.title: Senescent tumor cell membrane-based "time engine" nanosystem amplifies endoplasmic reticulum targeting for metastasis blockade.
delivery.subject: Science advances
delivery.reason: senescent-cell-membrane-coated nanoparticles sequentially amplify ER-targeted drug delivery
delivery.abstract: As an important component of biomimetic drug delivery systems, cell membrane-coated nanoparticles are widely used for subcellular delivery. However, the influence of cell membranes at different life cycles on subcellular delivery remains unexplored. Our previous study demonstrated that senescent tumor cell membrane-coated nanoparticles (SNP) displayed superior endoplasmic reticulum (ER) targeting efficiency in tumor cells. After inducing tumor cells into senescence, SNP showed greater accumulation in ER. Herein, we design a "time engine" nanosystem for amplified ER targeting: Firstly, ribociclib is encapsulated into SNP (R@SNP) to induce tumor cell senescence; then, SNP loaded with brefeldin A (B@SNP) is used to trigger ER stress. By sequential therapy, R@SNP disrupts the cytoskeleton of 4T1 tumor cells to eliminate ER-targeting barriers and remodels the tumor immune microenvironment; B@SNP boosts ER-targeting efficiency and triggers intense ER stress. Collectively, such time engine nanosystem achieves excellent ER accumulation and antimetastatic efficacy in 4T1 tumor-bearing mice, providing an innovative perspective for subcellular delivery and tumor treatment.

design-method.title: Inference-Time Steering Across Scaffolds and Epitopes for Sample-Efficient De Novo Nanobody Design
design-method.subject: cs.LG
design-method.reason: dynamic compute allocation across scaffolds/epitopes boosts nanobody design yield 5x
design-method.abstract: Generative molecular design typically relies on over-generation and post-hoc filtering. Inference-time steering methods like Feynman-Kac (FK) steering improve efficiency by biasing trajectories toward high-reward candidates, yet they optimize within a single fixed configuration. In de novo nanobody design, upfront commitment to conditioning choices like scaffold identity or target epitope creates a bottleneck. Since yield varies across these conditions, steering unpromising setups wastes compute. We recast generative condition selection as an inference-time resource-allocation problem. We propose two dynamic budget allocators: a joint Global Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) formulation that steers and allocates compute across configurations concurrently, and a decoupled approach adapting Batched Successive Elimination (BaSE). Empirically, these dynamic allocators increase the yield of designable candidates per GPU-hour nearly 5$\times$ without sacrificing diversity across distinct therapeutic targets and generative configurations.

design-method.title: Benchmarking interface confidence as a selection criterion for computational nanobody design against survivin's BIR-domain groove
design-method.subject: bioinformatics
design-method.reason: interface-confidence filtering shows no association with actual nanobody epitope engagement
design-method.abstract: Designed binders are routinely filtered on predicted interface confidence, which reports how self-consistently a model places an interface, not where it lies. We designed 200 nanobody loops against the survivin BIR-domain groove, co-folded 196, and checked epitope contact in every predicted complex. Confidence showed no detectable association with epitope engagement ({rho} = +0.100, 95% CI -0.04 to +0.24, n = 196); its highest and lowest quartiles failed alike (odds ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.41 to 2.26). It tracked instead the run's other confidence estimates ({rho} = +0.61). Twelve-seed replication separated two candidates the criteria had not: one reached the complete epitope in 10 of 12 runs, the other never. Across 155 predictions the top-ranked model was no better than one drawn at random from its five (P = 0.610), though only 3 of 31 failed on every model. Nothing was assayed; nb_cand_057 is an in silico candidate only.

design-method.title: PeTFlow: Flow-Matching Based All-Atom Peptide Design through Side-Chain State Tokenization
design-method.subject: biochemistry
design-method.reason: pocket-conditioned flow matching co-designs peptide sequence, conformation, interface via side-chain tokens
design-method.abstract: Peptide offers a powerful modality for targeting protein-protein interfaces, yet their computational design remains challenging because sequence identity, backbone geometry and side-chain packing must be optimized simultaneously within a three-dimensional pocket constrained environment. Here we present PeTFlow, a pocket-conditioned all-atom peptide co-design framework that rationalizes this constrained design problem through discrete side-chain state tokenization. In PeTFlow, each residue is represented as a chemically compatible state token, enabling unified modeling of peptide sequence, conformation and all-atom interface geometry. PeTFlow achieved superior generation quality on peptide-design benchmarks and can further be applied to therapeutically relevant peptide drug design.

design-method.title: Buried Ion-Pairs Reshape Folding Pathways of Artificial Proteins
design-method.authors_short: Liebau, J., …, Kaila, V. R. I.
design-method.subject: biophysics
design-method.reason: buried ion-pairs in de novo helical bundles reshape folding kinetic barriers
design-method.abstract: Ion-pairs are central charged motifs that control the biological function of several proteins. Yet, the physical principles linked to the formation of ion-pairs during protein folding remain poorly understood. Here, we show that buried ion-pairs of de novo-designed helical bundle proteins reshape the folding pathways by introducing kinetic barriers that are overcome by a hydrophobic collapse linked to packing of the protein core. By combining protein design with co-translational folding studies, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, and molecular dynamics simulations, we show that introduction of a buried ion-pair leads to a shifted folding transition that balances desolvation and electrostatic interactions within the protein and the bulk solvent. Moreover, we find that the folding pathway is sensitive to modifications in non-polar interactions and motifs that electrostatically shield the ion-pair from its surroundings. Our combined findings provide a blueprint for understanding how functional motifs affect protein folding and how mutation of charged networks alter the stability of proteins.

design-method.title: TopFor: Automated Preparation of AMBER-Compatible Parameters for Noncanonical Amino Acids in Peptides
design-method.authors_short: Buelbuel, E. F., …, Bozhueyuek, K. A. J.
design-method.subject: bioinformatics
design-method.reason: automates AMBER force-field parameterization for noncanonical-amino-acid peptide MD
design-method.abstract: Peptides containing noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) are becoming increasingly important in drug discovery, but their molecular dynamics (MD) simulation remains limited by labor-intensive residue parameterization and topology preparation. Here, we present TopFor (Topology and Residue Force-Field Parameter Preparation), an open-source, peptide-oriented workflow that automates the generation of ncAA residue templates and force-field parameter files for MD simulations with AMBER using established charge-derivation methods. TopFor supports single-residue, whole-peptide, and batch parameterization workflows. The workflow was validated using the MDM2-p53 complex by comparing native AMBER residue definitions with residues processed by TopFor using three charge-derivation methods, each evaluated in three independent 100 ns MD simulations. TopFor-generated residue definitions showed structural and conformational behavior comparable to the native AMBER representation. Applicability to more complex peptide architectures was demonstrated using the head-to-tail cyclic peptide cyclosporin A and the cyclic depsipeptide cyclohexylgriselimycin. At library scale, 1,138 of 1,214 cyclohexylgriselimycin derivatives (93.7%) successfully completed TopFor parameterization and the subsequent initial AMBER-based computational workflow across two derivatization campaigns. TopFor was further integrated into a structure-based peptide discovery workflow based on the DnaN-griselimycin complex. Six GM-derived peptides were computationally prioritized and experimentally evaluated, of which four produced SPR responses against Mycobacterium smegmatis (M. smegmatis) DnaN and three showed concentration-dependent responses. TopFor reduces the manual effort required to prepare ncAA-containing peptides for MD simulations and enables their integration into both library-scale computational screening and structure-based peptide discovery workflows.
